newsitem.title: UK: Labour to force UK water firms to mend leaks.
newsitem.headline: Labour to force UK water firms to mend leaks.

text.p: An incoming Labour government will require Britain's water companies to start an immediate emergency programme to mend leaks at their own expense, environment spokesman Frank Dobson said on Tuesday.
"Water companies will be told that, as an immediate step, they must start an immediate crash programme to mend leaks from customer pipes," he said in a statement.
"We would expect this to be a free service to customers including providing free telephone services for customers wishing to report leaks."
Dobson has promised to call an "emergency summit" on what it sees as Britain's water crisis bringing together water companies, industry regulators, and environmental and voluntary groups.
He said the companies would be ordered to start the leak programme at that summit.
"The companies should start to prepare for this crash programme now. We will expect them to present their plans to us at Labour's water summit. Excuses will not be tolerated," he added.

Dobson added the companies would be told that the new government would not grant licences for increased water abstraction from reservoirs or boreholes except where they could demonstrate that there was no alternative. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
